items.prose: Solve $ax + by = e$ and $cx + dy = f$ for $x$, by elimination. Each line carries its reason.
items.question: Put the lines of the derivation in order.

lines.text: $adx + bdy = ed$ and $bcx + bdy = bf$, multiply the first equation by $d$ and the second by $b$
$(ad - bc)x = ed - bf$, subtract the second from the first: the $bdy$ terms cancel
$x = \dfrac{ed - bf}{ad - bc}$, divide by $ad - bc$, allowed only when $ad - bc \neq 0$
$3x + 2y = 16$, $5x - 2y = 16$ give $x = \dfrac{-32 - 32}{-6 - 10} = 4$, a check against a pair solved earlier

items.title: Which broker, and when
items.prompt: Broker A charges £12.00 a month plus £0.40 per trade. Broker B has no monthly fee and charges £1.20 per trade. Write an equation for each broker's monthly cost with $n$ trades. Find the break-even number of trades and the cost there, with a reason for each step. Describe the two cost lines on a graph. Advise a trader who makes 10 trades a month and one who makes 30. Then Broker B cuts its rate to £0.40 per trade. Explain what happens to the break-even, using both the algebra and the graph.
items.model:
**Equations.** With $n$ trades a month, in pounds:

$$\begin{aligned} A &= 12 + 0.4n, \\ B &= 1.2n. \end{aligned}$$

**Break-even.** Set the costs equal and solve:

$$\begin{aligned} 12 + 0.4n &= 1.2n \\ &\quad \text{both brokers cost the same} \\ 12 &= 0.8n \\ &\quad \text{take } 0.4n \text{ from both sides} \\ n &= 15 \\ &\quad \text{divide both sides by } 0.8 \end{aligned}$$

At 15 trades both cost £18.00: $12 + 0.4 \times 15 = 18$ and $1.2 \times 15 = 18$.

**Graph.** Trades across, monthly cost up. Line A starts at £12.00 and climbs £0.40 per trade. Line B starts at £0.00 and climbs £1.20 per trade. B is steeper, so it catches A at the crossing $(15, 18)$. Left of the crossing B is lower; right of it A is lower.

**Advice.** At 10 trades: A costs £16.00 and B £12.00, so B is cheaper. At 30 trades: A costs £24.00 and B £36.00, so A is cheaper. The break-even of 15 trades is the dividing line.

**B cuts to £0.40.** Now $B = 0.4n$. Setting $12 + 0.4n = 0.4n$ and taking $0.4n$ from both sides gives $12 = 0$, which is false. So there is no break-even. On the graph the two lines now have the same gradient, 0.4, and start £12.00 apart: they are parallel and never meet. B is cheaper by exactly £12.00 for every number of trades.

rubric.text: Writes both cost equations with $n$ defined and units stated: $A = 12 + 0.4n$, $B = 1.2n$.
Solves $12 + 0.4n = 1.2n$ to $n = 15$ with a reason for each step.
Gives the cost at break-even, £18.00, checked in both equations.
Describes the graph: both intercepts, both gradients, the crossing at $(15, 18)$, and which line is lower on each side.
Advises correctly with numbers: 10 trades, B at £12.00 against £16.00; 30 trades, A at £24.00 against £36.00.
For the £0.40 rate: reaches the false line $12 = 0$, names the lines as parallel, and concludes B is always £12.00 cheaper.
